scope: iPad environment configuration parity with supported Mac manager settings; original shared TOML/authorization codec, no guest locale changes or execution/coordinator redesign.
implementation: Per-environment CPU, memory, startup/session, native components and host/no-network controls.
TOML draft edit/import/export and fresh identity on creation.
Single allow/deny control per supported capability, independent local grant and OS/Files authority.
Lossless schema tree and original Boolean serialization; validation before writes, stale-write rejection and best-effort I/O rollback.
Saved settings apply on next start, including normal Debian preparation.
Configured auto memory uses host-managed limits and original provider callback with actual host metadata; no new thread, polling or fixed guest pool.
New environment creation remains stopped and keeps primary action visible above the keyboard.
Current environment stop/restart uses the existing workspace lifecycle; no data reset or new runtime control path.

cases: Independent profiles, persisted systemd setup flag, fresh imported identity and non-escalating editor merge.
Locale catalogs and existing clipboard transfer with former app-global Bridge disabled.
Chinese CPU/memory/permission save, other-environment isolation, discard/cancel, relaunch persistence.
English Android configuration and actual environment creation with portrait soft keyboard visible.

limits: One local iPad environment runs at a time; opening another stops the previous runtime.
Bridge/port publishing, host command/CLI and direct host folder mounts remain unavailable on iPad.
Permissions and configuration edits apply on next start, not live revocation.
Configuration/grant/catalog replacement is atomic per file, not a multi-file power-loss transaction.
Physical-iPad live behavior and audio capture were not tested in this iteration.
